PRODUCT RECALL NOTICE
Issued by the Local Vehicle and Trade Safety Office (LVTSO)
Reference No: LVTSO-REC-2024-001
Date of Issue: 5 January 2024
Effective Date: Immediate

RECALL OF 'ACME TURBO CHARGER'

Gippsland Community Marketplace product_recall_notice Recall of 'ACME Turbo Charger' due to overheating risk. Record status: current.

This notice is issued to inform all consumers, retailers, and marketplace participants of a voluntary recall of the ACME Turbo Charger (model numbers AT-100, AT-200, AT-300). The recall has been initiated following reports of the product overheating during use, which may pose a fire hazard and risk of burns to users.

Products Affected:
The recall applies to all units of the ACME Turbo Charger sold through Gippsland Community Marketplace between 1 March 2023 and 20 December 2023. This includes units purchased as standalone items and those bundled with other products. The affected model numbers are listed above; no other ACME products are included in this recall.

Reason for Recall:
Testing conducted by LVTSO has identified that the ACME Turbo Charger can overheat under normal operating conditions, particularly when used continuously for extended periods. In some reported cases, the outer casing has reached temperatures that could cause minor burns upon contact. There have been no reports of serious injury or property damage to date, but the risk is considered significant enough to warrant immediate action.

What Consumers Should Do:
If you have purchased an ACME Turbo Charger from Gippsland Community Marketplace, you should immediately stop using the product and unplug it from any power source. Do not attempt to repair or modify the charger yourself. Please return the product to the point of purchase or contact the marketplace's customer service team for a full refund or replacement.

Retailers and sellers on Gippsland Community Marketplace are required to remove all affected units from sale and to contact LVTSO to arrange for collection or disposal of stock. Any seller who has sold an affected unit should also notify their buyers directly and provide information about the recall.

Contact Details:
For further information about this recall, or to arrange a return, please contact:
LVTSO Consumer Safety Line: 1800 555 019
Email: recalls@lvsto.vic.gov.au
Website: www.lvtso.vic.gov.au/recalls

Alternatively, you may contact Gippsland Community Marketplace directly at:
Customer Support: 1300 789 456
Email: support@gippslandmarketplace.com.au

Please have your order number or proof of purchase ready when contacting us. This will help us process your request more quickly.

Standard Safety Advice:
LVTSO reminds all consumers to regularly check for product recall notices and safety warnings before using any electrical products, particularly those purchased through online marketplaces. To stay informed, you can:
- Visit the LVTSO website and subscribe to recall alerts.
- Check the product registration database for your appliances and devices.
- Register your purchases with the manufacturer where possible, so you can be notified of any future recalls.

Consumers who have experienced any issues with the ACME Turbo Charger, including overheating, smoke, or unusual odours, are encouraged to report these incidents to LVTSO. Your reports help us identify potential hazards and take prompt action to protect the community.

LVTSO also advises that all electrical products should be used in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. Do not leave chargers plugged in unattended for long periods, and always use them on a flat, non-flammable surface with adequate ventilation.

This recall is being conducted in cooperation with the manufacturer and Gippsland Community Marketplace. Further updates will be provided on the LVTSO website as new information becomes available.

Authorised by:
[Signature]
Margaret Chen
Director, Consumer Safety Division
Local Vehicle and Trade Safety Office
Date: 5 January 2024

End of Notice.
To determine whether your charger is affected, please follow these steps:

1. Unplug the charger from the power outlet and allow it to cool for at least 10 minutes.
2. Turn the charger over and locate the white label or the serial number on the side panel.
3. Compare the batch code or serial number with the list above.
4. If your unit matches, stop using it immediately and follow the return instructions below.

If you are unsure whether your unit is affected, err on the side of caution and treat it as affected. Do not continue using the charger while waiting for confirmation.

What LVTSO Is Doing

LVTSO has issued this recall in cooperation with the manufacturer, ACME Manufacturing Pty Ltd, and the online marketplace Gippsland Community Marketplace. The manufacturer has agreed to provide a full refund or a replacement unit of equivalent value, at the consumer's choice. All shipping costs associated with the return will be borne by the manufacturer; consumers will not be out of pocket.

The enforcement action code for this matter is INF-2024-001. This code should be quoted in all correspondence with LVTSO or the manufacturer regarding this recall. It assists our office in tracking enquiries and ensuring that responses are directed to the correct team.

What Consumers Should Do

If you own an affected ACME Turbo Charger, please take the following steps:

- Immediately stop using the charger and unplug it from the power source.
- Do not attempt to repair the unit yourself or have it repaired by an unauthorised service centre.
- Contact the LVTSO Consumer Safety Line on 1800 555 019 or email recalls@lvsto.vic.gov.au to arrange for the return of your unit.
- Alternatively, you may contact Gippsland Community Marketplace directly on 1300 789 456 or at support@gippslandmarketplace.com.au. Please quote the enforcement action code INF-2024-001 when contacting either organisation.
- Have your order number or proof of purchase ready, as this will expedite the return process. If you no longer have your proof of purchase, you may still be eligible for a refund; please contact us to discuss your options.

Latrobe Valley Trading Standards Office enforcement action code: INF-2024-001. Record status: current.

Refund and Replacement Process

Once your affected unit has been received and verified, you will be offered a full refund of the purchase price or a replacement unit, free of charge. Refunds will be processed within 10 business days of receipt of the returned unit. Replacements will be dispatched within 15 business days, subject to stock availability. If you choose a replacement and the model is no longer available, an equivalent model will be offered.

Consumers who purchased the ACME Turbo Charger as a gift and do not have the original receipt should still contact LVTSO or Gippsland Community Marketplace. We will work with you to verify the purchase date and eligibility.

Retailer Obligations

All retailers and marketplace sellers who have sold the ACME Turbo Charger are required to:

- Remove affected units from their online listings and physical shelves immediately.
- Notify all purchasers of affected units directly, providing them with a copy of this notice or a link to the LVTSO website.
- Maintain records of all sales of affected units for a period of at least 12 months, in case further contact with purchasers is required.

Failure to comply with these obligations may result in further enforcement action by LVTSO, including the imposition of penalties under the Consumer Goods (Product Safety) Regulations.

Reporting Incidents

Consumers who have experienced any issues with the ACME Turbo Charger, including overheating, smoke, unusual odours, or visible damage to the unit, are strongly encouraged to report these incidents to LVTSO. Reports can be made through the LVTSO website (www.lvtso.vic.gov.au/recalls) or by calling the Consumer Safety Line. Please include the batch code or serial number of your unit, the date of the incident, and a description of what occurred. Photographs of any damage are also helpful.
**Other Recent Recalls and Safety Warnings**

For the information of consumers and retailers, the following recalls and safety warnings have been issued by LVTSO in recent months. These matters are separate from the ACME Turbo Charger recall and are listed for general awareness.

**1. Bella Homewares – Ceramic Cookware Set (Model: BellaStone 12-Piece)**

- **Date of Issue:** 18 November 2023
- **Reference Number:** LVTSO-REC-2023-087
- **Status:** Current
- **Description:** The ceramic coating on these pans may chip or flake during normal use. Small fragments have been reported in food. Consumers are advised to stop using the affected products immediately and contact the importer for a refund or replacement. Affected batch codes begin with "BS23".

**2. EcoGlow – Rechargeable LED Lantern (Model: EG-400)**

- **Date of Issue:** 2 December 2023
- **Reference Number:** LVTSO-REC-2023-094
- **Status:** Current
- **Description:** A fault in the charging circuit may cause the lantern to overheat while charging, posing a fire hazard. The product was sold through several online marketplaces and camping supply stores. Consumers should unplug the lantern and return it to the point of purchase for a full refund.

**3. KidsPlay – Wooden Activity Cube (Model: KP-112)**

- **Date of Issue:** 15 December 2023
- **Reference Number:** LVTSO-REC-2023-101
- **Status:** Current
- **Description:** Small wooden pegs on the activity cube may detach, presenting a choking hazard for young children. The product was sold between March and November 2023. Consumers are urged to keep the toy away from children and contact KidsPlay for a replacement or refund.

**4. VoltEdge – USB Wall Charger (Model: VE-20W)**

- **Date of Issue:** 22 December 2023
- **Reference Number:** LVTSO-REC-2023-108
- **Status:** Current
- **Description:** The charger may fail to meet Australian electrical safety standards due to insufficient insulation. There is a risk of electric shock. The charger was sold online and in discount variety stores. Consumers should stop using the charger immediately and dispose of it or return it for a refund.

**5. FreshFlow – Stainless Steel Water Bottle (Model: FF-750)**

- **Date of Issue:** 29 December 2023
- **Reference Number:** LVTSO-REC-2023-115
- **Status:** Current
- **Description:** The vacuum seal on some bottles may fail, causing the outer wall to become very hot when filled with hot liquids. This poses a burn risk. The affected bottles have batch codes "FF23-07" through "FF23-09". Refunds are available from the distributor.

**6. SunRay – Portable Gas Heater (Model: SR-2000)**

- **Date of Issue:** 4 January 2024
- **Reference Number:** LVTSO-REC-2024-001
- **Status:** Current
- **Description:** A potential gas leak at the regulator connection has been identified. This presents a fire and explosion hazard. The heater was sold at outdoor markets and through a small number of online retailers. Consumers should immediately turn off the gas supply and do not use the heater. Contact the supplier for a full refund.

**Important Note on the Above Items**

The recalls listed above are separate from the ACME Turbo Charger recall. If you have purchased any of these products, please follow the instructions provided in each individual notice. Further details for each recall can be found on the LVTSO website under the specific reference number.

**General Consumer Safety Advice**

LVTSO reminds all consumers to register their products with manufacturers where possible, as this helps ensure you are notified directly of any future recalls. When purchasing goods online, check that the seller is reputable and that the product displays appropriate Australian regulatory markings where applicable. If you are unsure whether a product you own is affected by a recall, err on the side of caution and stop using it until you have verified its status.

**Contacting LVTSO**

If you have any questions about the recalls listed above, or any other product safety matter, please do not hesitate to contact us.
LVTSO-REC-2024-002
Issued: 5 January 2024
Effective: Immediately

**Product Recall Notice: ACME Turbo Charger (Model: TC-500)**

This notice supersedes the preliminary warning issued on 2 January 2024 (Reference LVTSO-ADV-2024-003). The preliminary warning was based on initial laboratory findings; further testing has confirmed the fault and its scope, and the formal recall details below now apply.

---

**1. Product and Identifying Details**

- **Product:** ACME Turbo Charger
- **Model Number:** TC-500
- **Batch Codes:** TC-24-01 through TC-24-06
- **Period of Sale:** 1 October 2023 to 28 December 2023
- **Places of Sale:** Sold exclusively through the ACME online store (www.acme.example.com.au) and via the ACME authorised reseller network on third-party marketplaces. A small number of units were sold through two retail outlets in New South Wales and Victoria.

**2. Description of the Defect**

Internal testing and subsequent investigation have identified that the thermal fuse inside the charger may fail to operate as designed under certain conditions of prolonged high-voltage fluctuation. In a small number of reported cases, the charger has continued to deliver power after the connected device reached full charge, leading to overheating of the charging unit. No injuries have been reported to LVTSO at the time of issue, but the potential for fire exists if the unit is left unattended while charging.

**3. Hazard**

- Overheating of the charger unit
- Potential for melting of the outer casing
- Potential fire hazard

**4. What Consumers Should Do**

Consumers who purchased an ACME Turbo Charger (Model TC-500) with a batch code listed above should:

- Stop using the charger immediately and unplug it from the power outlet.
- Do not attempt to repair the charger or replace the fuse.
- Return the charger to the place of purchase for a full refund. No proof of purchase is required.
- Alternatively, contact ACME directly via the details below to arrange a prepaid return parcel.

For consumers who purchased through the ACME online store, a refund will be processed automatically upon receipt of the returned unit. For purchases made through authorised resellers on third-party marketplaces, contact the seller directly for return instructions.

**5. Refund and Contact Details**

- **ACME Customer Support (Australia):** 1800 555 014 (Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM AEDT)
- **Email:** recall@acme.example.com.au
- **Web:** www.acme.example.com.au/recall-tc500
- **Postal:** ACME Pty Ltd, Locked Bag 4000, Sydney NSW 2001

When contacting ACME, please have the batch code (printed on the underside of the charger) ready. ACME has committed to processing all refunds within 10 business days of receiving the returned product.

**6. Regulatory Action**

This recall has been coordinated with LVTSO. The manufacturer has agreed to:

- Cease all sales of the affected batch codes.
- Notify all known purchasers via email using the contact details held on file.
- Provide a corrective action report to LVTSO within 30 days of this notice.

LVTSO will continue to monitor the recall and may issue further updates if additional affected batch codes are identified.

---

**Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q1: How do I know if my charger is affected?**
Check the batch code printed on the underside of the charger. If the code begins with "TC-24-" and the last two digits are between 01 and 06, your unit is affected. If the batch code is not visible or has worn off, treat the unit as affected and do not use it.

**Q2: I bought my charger as a gift. Can I still get a refund?**
Yes. No proof of purchase is required. The refund will be issued to the person returning the unit. If you are returning a gift on behalf of the recipient, you may do so.

**Q3: What if I no longer have the original packaging or the receipt?**
The original packaging and receipt are not required. Only the charger itself needs to be returned.

**Q4: Is the charger safe to use for a few more days while I arrange the return?**
No. LVTSO advises that you stop using the charger immediately and unplug it. The risk of overheating increases with continued use, particularly during longer charging sessions.

This memo summarises the proposed updates to the Marketplace Safety Policy, specifically around high-risk second-hand goods listings, and captures the meeting notes and action items from the 12 January 2024 working group session. The proposal is currently in the review phase.

The proposed update introduces a mandatory pre-approval step for listings in the following categories: child car seats, bicycle helmets, and e-scooter batteries. **Important context:** This is a proposal. It has not been approved. The current live policy (v4.2, dated 02/11/2023) remains in effect and does not require pre-approval for these categories. PRODUCT RECALL NOTICE
Issued by the Local Vehicle and Trade Safety Office (LVTSO)
Reference No: LVTSO-REC-2024-001
Date of Issue: 5 January 2024
Effective Date: Immediate

RECALL OF 'ACME TURBO CHARGER'

Gippsland Community Marketplace product_recall_notice Recall of 'ACME Turbo Charger' due to overheating risk. Record status: current.

This notice is issued to inform all consumers, retailers, and marketplace participants of a voluntary recall of the ACME Turbo Charger (model numbers AT-100, AT-200, AT-300). The recall has been initiated following reports of the product overheating during use, which may pose a fire hazard and risk of burns to users.

Products Affected:
The recall applies to all units of the ACME Turbo Charger sold through Gippsland Community Marketplace between 1 March 2023 and 20 December 2023. This includes units purchased as standalone items and those bundled with other products. The affected model numbers are listed above; no other ACME products are included in this recall.

Reason for Recall:
Testing conducted by LVTSO has identified that the ACME Turbo Charger can overheat under normal operating conditions, particularly when used continuously for extended periods. In some reported cases, the outer casing has reached temperatures that could cause minor burns upon contact. There have been no reports of serious injury or property damage to date, but the risk is considered significant enough to warrant immediate action.

What Consumers Should Do:
If you have purchased an ACME Turbo Charger from Gippsland Community Marketplace, you should immediately stop using the product and unplug it from any power source. Do not attempt to repair or modify the charger yourself. Please return the product to the point of purchase or contact the marketplace's customer service team for a full refund or replacement.

Retailers and sellers on Gippsland Community Marketplace are required to remove all affected units from sale and to contact LVTSO to arrange for collection or disposal of stock. Any seller who has sold an affected unit should also notify their buyers directly and provide information about the recall.

Contact Details:
For further information about this recall, or to arrange a return, please contact:
LVTSO Consumer Safety Line: 1800 555 019
Email: recalls@lvsto.vic.gov.au
Website: www.lvtso.vic.gov.au/recalls

Alternatively, you may contact Gippsland Community Marketplace directly at:
Customer Support: 1300 789 456
Email: support@gippslandmarketplace.com.au

Please have your order number or proof of purchase ready when contacting us. This will help us process your request more quickly.

Standard Safety Advice:
LVTSO reminds all consumers to regularly check for product recall notices and safety warnings before using any electrical products, particularly those purchased through online marketplaces. To stay informed, you can:
- Visit the LVTSO website and subscribe to recall alerts.
- Check the product registration database for your appliances and devices.
- Register your purchases with the manufacturer where possible, so you can be notified of any future recalls.

Consumers who have experienced any issues with the ACME Turbo Charger, including overheating, smoke, or unusual odours, are encouraged to report these incidents to LVTSO. Your reports help us identify potential hazards and take prompt action to protect the community.

LVTSO also advises that all electrical products should be used in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. Do not leave chargers plugged in unattended for long periods, and always use them on a flat, non-flammable surface with adequate ventilation.

This recall is being conducted in cooperation with the manufacturer and Gippsland Community Marketplace. Further updates will be provided on the LVTSO website as new information becomes available.

Authorised by:
[Signature]
Margaret Chen
Director, Consumer Safety Division
Local Vehicle and Trade Safety Office
Date: 5 January 2024

End of Notice.

LVTSO-REC-2024-002
Issued: 5 January 2024
Effective: Immediately

**Product Recall Notice: ACME Turbo Charger (Model: TC-500)**

This notice supersedes the preliminary warning issued on 2 January 2024 (Reference LVTSO-ADV-2024-003). The preliminary warning was based on initial laboratory findings; further testing has confirmed the fault and its scope, and the formal recall details below now apply.

---

**1. Product and Identifying Details**

- **Product:** ACME Turbo Charger
- **Model Number:** TC-500
- **Batch Codes:** TC-24-01 through TC-24-06
- **Period of Sale:** 1 October 2023 to 28 December 2023
- **Places of Sale:** Sold exclusively through the ACME online store (www.acme.example.com.au) and via the ACME authorised reseller network on third-party marketplaces. A small number of units were sold through two retail outlets in New South Wales and Victoria.

**2. Description of the Defect**

Internal testing and subsequent investigation have identified that the thermal fuse inside the charger may fail to operate as designed under certain conditions of prolonged high-voltage fluctuation. In a small number of reported cases, the charger has continued to deliver power after the connected device reached full charge, leading to overheating of the charging unit. No injuries have been reported to LVTSO at the time of issue, but the potential for fire exists if the unit is left unattended while charging.

**3. Hazard**

- Overheating of the charger unit
- Potential for melting of the outer casing
- Potential fire hazard

**4. What Consumers Should Do**

Consumers who purchased an ACME Turbo Charger (Model TC-500) with a batch code listed above should:

- Stop using the charger immediately and unplug it from the power outlet.
- Do not attempt to repair the charger or replace the fuse.
- Return the charger to the place of purchase for a full refund. No proof of purchase is required.
- Alternatively, contact ACME directly via the details below to arrange a prepaid return parcel.

For consumers who purchased through the ACME online store, a refund will be processed automatically upon receipt of the returned unit. For purchases made through authorised resellers on third-party marketplaces, contact the seller directly for return instructions.

**5. Refund and Contact Details**

- **ACME Customer Support (Australia):** 1800 555 014 (Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM AEDT)
- **Email:** recall@acme.example.com.au
- **Web:** www.acme.example.com.au/recall-tc500
- **Postal:** ACME Pty Ltd, Locked Bag 4000, Sydney NSW 2001

When contacting ACME, please have the batch code (printed on the underside of the charger) ready. ACME has committed to processing all refunds within 10 business days of receiving the returned product.

**6. Regulatory Action**

This recall has been coordinated with LVTSO. The manufacturer has agreed to:

- Cease all sales of the affected batch codes.
- Notify all known purchasers via email using the contact details held on file.
- Provide a corrective action report to LVTSO within 30 days of this notice.

LVTSO will continue to monitor the recall and may issue further updates if additional affected batch codes are identified.

---

**Frequently Asked Questions**

**Q1: How do I know if my charger is affected?**
Check the batch code printed on the underside of the charger. If the code begins with "TC-24-" and the last two digits are between 01 and 06, your unit is affected. If the batch code is not visible or has worn off, treat the unit as affected and do not use it.

**Q2: I bought my charger as a gift. Can I still get a refund?**
Yes. No proof of purchase is required. The refund will be issued to the person returning the unit. If you are returning a gift on behalf of the recipient, you may do so.

**Q3: What if I no longer have the original packaging or the receipt?**
The original packaging and receipt are not required. Only the charger itself needs to be returned.

**Q4: Is the charger safe to use for a few more days while I arrange the return?**
No. LVTSO advises that you stop using the charger immediately and unplug it. The risk of overheating increases with continued use, particularly during longer charging sessions.

4. **Definition of "household batteries":** The approved wording from L. Chen is included in the declaration. **Safety tips you can use today**

While the workshop covers each topic in detail, here are a few simple reminders from our educators to get you started:

- **Car seats:** The harness should be snug – you should not be able to pinch any webbing at the shoulder. If the seat moves more than 2.5 cm at the belt path, it is not tight enough.
- **Poison storage:** Keep all cleaning products, medicines, and laundry detergent in a locked cupboard above waist height. Never store them under the sink or on a low shelf.
- **Water safety:** Always actively supervise children around water. Drowning is fast and silent – it does not look like it does on TV. Empty paddling pools and buckets after use and store them upside down.
- **Home safety:** Secure heavy furniture, TVs, and bookshelves to the wall. A child can pull a chest of drawers over themselves by climbing the open drawers. Use furniture anchors on anything over 60 cm tall.
- **Helmets:** A helmet should sit level on the head, about two finger-widths above the eyebrows. The straps should form a V under the ears and be snug under the chin. Replace any helmet after a crash, even if it looks fine.
